reproduction: probes/p70_tls_env.py: with only SSL_CERT_FILE=<repo>/adapters/adapter_tests/fixtures/tls/test-ca.pem in the environment, the UNMODIFIED production tls_context() completes a handshake with the committed leaf (SAN api.oddspapi.io) and the keyed request line (apiKey=...) reaches the server; control without the variable: NO_RESPONSE. `openssl x509`: CA unconstrained, valid 2026-2046; leaf private key committed.
expected: No test certificate/key can create a production trust bypass; release exclusion is enforced, not documented.
actual: No CLI option or production import references the material (HA-13 fix), but the environment redirects the production trust store to the committed CA; the leaf private key for the production host name is public in the repository and history; export-ignore protects only `git archive`; no packaging/release check exists.

minimal_remediation_requirement: Live CLI refuses to run when SSL_CERT_FILE/SSL_CERT_DIR (and other trust-store overrides) are set, or tls_context() loads the system store without environment overrides; do not commit a private key whose certificate names the production host (generate the loopback CA/leaf at test time, non-production SAN + explicit server_hostname, or constrain/shorten the CA and drop the leaf key); enforce release exclusion with a test.
required_regression: p70 scenario ends in refusal/SSLCertVerificationError; test fails if any private-key block exists under adapters/ or if fixtures/tls/** is reachable from a built archive/distribution.

architecture_citation: §14.6 rule 3 (hard transport deadline for the whole attempt: connect, TLS, write, response read; at the deadline the connection is aborted and the attempt records NO_RESPONSE/TRUNCATED); BND-04
code_location: adapters/src/genesis_adapters/oddspapi/transport_http.py:77-81 (read_chunk -> response.read(size) blocks until size bytes), :217-225 (loop re-arms the socket timeout per call, not per recv)
reproduction: probes/p11_slowdrip.py: real loopback TLS server drips a 59-byte Content-Length body at 0.7 s/byte; deadline 3 s -> send() returned after 40.62 s with outcome RESPONSE and T1 37 s after the deadline. probes/p10_deadline.py shows the fake-connection cases (a-g) the existing tests cover.
expected: Attempt aborted at Tq+request_timeout_seconds regardless of how the peer paces bytes.
actual: Each recv gets a fresh timeout, so a peer sending one byte per (timeout-eps) extends the exchange indefinitely (bounded only by max_response_bytes). The runner later discards the late body (DeadlineExceeded) but only after the single writer, holding the run lock, was held.
consequence: Availability/hang by a slow or hostile provider; accounting window attribution is NOT affected (the request was written before the deadline). Mutants M03/M04 (connect/read deadline branches removed) survive the suite: BND-04 uses fakes, not a socket.
minimal_remediation_requirement: Enforce an absolute bound on every read (select/non-blocking reads recomputing the remaining time per read, or a watchdog that closes the socket at the deadline).
required_regression: Real-socket slow-drip test: total body time > deadline => send() returns by deadline+epsilon with NO_RESPONSE/TRUNCATED, never RESPONSE; kills mutants M03/M04.
